## Design

### 2026-11-08: Date: November 7, 2026

**3h**

Date: November 7, 2026

In this session, I designed the main body of the train, including the smokestack, boiler, and wheels. Since I wanted the whole design to look like it could be assembled, I designed some screw-like connecting pieces to attach to the connection pieces. On the back of the main body, I designed a small hitch with a pin that can be used to connect other cars to the main body. I find designing the body to be a bit difficult because some parts needed specific measurements to get the proportions right, so I had to try multiple dimensions to get the appearance that I wanted. Some of the Onshape tools that I used were extrude, fillet, hole, revolve, loft, and offset planes. I also used the appearance tool to customize the colors of the parts. In the next session, I will continue with the linkage rod designs and cow catcher design along with a track.

### 2026-11-08: Date: November 8, 2026

**4h**

Date: November 8, 2026

In this session, I continued designing the connection parts, including the axle peg, linkage peg, linkage rod, cow catcher, and track. The cow catcher took a little more time because I had to take precise measurements to ensure it could attach to the front of the train without any issues. After all the parts were finished, I went into the assembly page to put everything together. After that, I went a bit further and explored how to use orthographic drawings and exploded drawings to make sort of like a blueprint of my design.
